description: The Syrian Tetrapolis was a group of four major Hellenistic cities in northern Syria—Antioch, Seleucia Pieria, Apamea, and Laodicea—founded or greatly developed under the Seleucid dynasty. Together they formed the political, military, commercial, and cultural heart of Seleucid Syria, linking the Mediterranean coast with inland trade routes and the royal centers of the empire. Each city had a distinct role, with Antioch serving as the principal royal capital, Seleucia as its port, Apamea as an important military and administrative center, and Laodicea as a coastal commercial hub.
